newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close lower, finance concerns linger.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close lower, finance concerns linger.

text.p: Battered Thai stocks declined for a fourth day in a row on Thursday as investors sold on lingering concerns over prospects for finance company earnings after an industry shake up this week, brokers said.

The SET index finished 7.07 points lower at 676.65 on moderate trade of about five billion baht turnover. It was the lowest close since May 19, 1992, when the index finished at 667.84. The SET-50 index ended 0.52 point down at 49.38.
Decliners led gainers 201 to 125 while 82 issues unchanged.

The SET composite index moved in a narrrow range throughout the session on Thursday as most investors remained on the sidelines awaiting fresh and positive news which would enable them to enter the market.

"No positive news was seen in the market at all today. Investors were still shocked with a new government measures requiring commercial banks and finance firms to raise provisions for sub-standard assets," said a broker at Securities One.
Brokers said the order which was imposed by the central bank on Monday had worried investors as they believed it would affect liquidity of finance firms.
Brokers said the suspension this week of three senior Bank of Thailand officials, including its deputy governor Jaroong Nookhwun, by the government had also concerned investors.
The officials were suspended in connection with their failure to bring former executives of the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce to court for violations of the Banking Act.
"The stock market has been bad for quite a while already. This suspension action came at a wrong timing. It's just like rubbing salt in the wounds," said one broker.
Dhana Siam Finance topped the active list, falling three baht to 36.25, Thai Farmers Bank gained one to 110 and large capitalised Siam Cement declined 32 to 624.
In the communication sector, United Communication advanced one baht to 157 and TelecomAsia rose 0.25 to 38.25.
